body.statement: Derive an explicit rate \(r_n(\alpha,\beta,\gamma,d)\), including every phase boundary and every necessary equality-case logarithm, and prove \(c_{\mathrm{rate}}r_n\le\rho_\star(n)\le C_{\mathrm{rate}}r_n\) over the observed image \(\mathcal P^{\mathrm{obs}}\) for every \(n\ge n_0\). The upper inequality must be attained by a total data-computable test with uniform size and power; the lower inequality must hold for all randomized tests via priors on observed laws in \(\mathcal P^{\mathrm{obs}}\) whose full-law null lifts each have constant \(\tau^{\mathrm F}\) and exact uniform design. Determine from the derived formula whether \(r_n=r_{\mathrm{or}}\), and exactly where learning \(e\) and \(\mu_0\) changes the benchmark; \(R_{\mathrm{up}}\) is one candidate upper bound and is not prescribed as the answer.
body.justification: The same-class converse is the theorem-level kernel; it decides whether rough confounding genuinely alters omnibus detectability rather than merely degrading a particular estimator.
body.gap: KennedyBalakrishnanRobinsWasserman2024 proves a nuisance elbow for pointwise CATE estimation, while KotekalKundu2025 proves a rough-mean elbow for heteroskedasticity testing; neither supplies constant-CATE testing priors that preserve this model's baseline smoothness and exact uniform design.
body.consumer: A sharp answer identifies when dScoreTest's first-order hunting route can be omnibus-rate optimal and when a higher-order calibrated alternative is statistically necessary.

obligation.what_is_open: Whether the nuisance-limited upper endpoint is the full-class minimax separation rate when \(\alpha+\beta<2d\gamma/(4\gamma+d)\), including any logarithm at a genuinely sharp equality boundary.
obligation.obstruction: The oracle Bernoulli bump mixture proves only the oracle endpoint. A nuisance-scale converse needs a prior whose every null draw has constant CATE, whose alternatives obey the separate propensity, baseline, and CATE Hölder restrictions, and whose complete four-cell observed likelihood remains close under exact uniform design. The available local moment-matching idea does not control the observed transition regions and may make the alternative baseline inherit impermissible CATE roughness when \(\beta>\gamma\).
obligation.attempted: The corrected projection upper bound was fully audited for unrelated ranks, including the prescribed case \(d=1\), \(\alpha=1/64\), \(\beta=9/64\), \(\gamma=1/8\), where the candidate tuning has \(k\asymp n^{40/31}\) and \(\ell\asymp n^{32/31}\). The dimension-free coefficient covariance and uniform quadratic profiling remain valid there, and the standard oracle sign-mixture calculation was completed. The local correlated propensity-baseline perturbation was not promoted to a lower bound because it neither matches all observed Bernoulli cell probabilities nor controls transition-region mass under the fixed uniform design.
obligation.partial_result:
The fully verified result is
\[
 c\,n^{-2\gamma/(4\gamma+d)}
 \le\rho_\star(n)
 \le C\left\{n^{-2\gamma/(4\gamma+d)}
 \vee n^{-4\gamma(\alpha+\beta)/[4\gamma(\alpha+\beta)+d(\alpha+\beta)+2d\gamma]}\right\}.
\]
The upper test is the finite corrected-energy test proved above and the lower endpoint follows by information monotonicity from the legal oracle Bernoulli mixture.  The endpoints match when \(\alpha+\beta\ge2d\gamma/(4\gamma+d)\), yielding the oracle rate there.  When the inequality is strict in the other direction, no legal composite-null mixture at the nuisance endpoint has been established, so the exact rate and any equality-case logarithm remain open.
